channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Molecular Cell, Nature Structural & Molecular Biology, and The EMBO Journal.

item.title: Molecular Cell: A protein-dependent riboswitch activates ribosomal frameshifting in cardioviruses
item.description: Betts et al. investigate how the viral 2A protein controls programmed −1 ribosomal frameshifting (PRF) in cardioviruses. Their findings reveal an unexpected protein-dependent riboswitch mechanism, providing new insights into how frameshifting can be conditionally activated and establishing the remodeling of structured RNA as a regulatory principle in viral translational control.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Nicotinamide nucleotide transhydrogenase directly couples redox homeostasis to proline biosynthesis in human glioma
item.description: Vettore and Boufersaoui et al. show that glioma cells require efficient regeneration of mitochondrial NADPH through the enzyme nicotinamide nucleotide transhydrogenase (NNT) to adapt to metabolic and redox challenges in hypoxia. Glioma cells lacking sufficient NNT activity have strongly impaired growth in vitro and in vivo.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Anchoring of perforin-2 via the transmembrane domain is required for antigen escape into the cytosol
Molecular Cell: Acidic transcription factors position the genome at nuclear speckles through transcription -dependent and -independent mechanisms
item.description: Chaturvedi et al. demonstrate that acidic transcription factors reposition genomic loci to nuclear speckles through both transcription-dependent and transcription-independent mechanisms, revealing that speckle association is actively established by cis-regulatory DNA elements and transcription factor properties rather than arising simply as a consequence of active gene expression.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Hydrophobic interactions of FG-nucleoporins are required for dilating nuclear membrane pores into selective transport channels after mitosis
item.description: Zhang et al. show that FG-nucleoporins self-assemble through hydrophobic interactions to dilate newly assembling nuclear pores after mitosis, enabling nuclear import and nuclear expansion, which in turn remodel the nuclear envelope.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Disease-specific tau polymorphs are associated with unique protein networks across proteinopathies
Molecular Cell: Maintenance of nucleosome organization through replication and transcription counteracts aberrant coalescence of active chromatin
item.description: Frater et al. show an essential role of mammalian FACT in coordinating replisome and RNA polymerase progression through chromatin with histone recycling to maintain histone modifications. They further demonstrate that losing nucleosome organization can dynamically regulate chromatin compartmentalization.

item.title: Molecular Cell: ER-liquid condensate contacts sequester FAM134B/C and RhoA to govern cell morphology
item.description: Jimenez-Moreno et al. reveal that ER-phagy receptors directly control cytosolic signaling events. Upon stimulation, cytoplasmic PRKAR1A condensates interact with FAM134B/C, forming inter-organellar contacts that bridge the ER and lysosomes into a localized hydrolytic hub. This hub drives the degradation of RhoA, coordinating morphology transitions during cancer cell invasion.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Excess intracellular lactate represses mRNA translation and tumor progression through lactate-tRNA charging
item.description: Wang et al. reveal a metabolite-tRNA charging mechanism that links metabolic state directly to translational control. Intracellular lactate accumulation directly represses mRNA translation via lactate-tRNA charging mediated by AARS1, uncovering an intrinsic metabolic brake that aggressive tumors evade by exporting lactate and identifying a therapeutic vulnerability to suppress cancer cell fitness.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Pervasive noise in human pre-mRNA splice site selection
item.description: Human splicing is noisy, with cryptic splicing at both high- and low-fidelity motifs, associated with features that probabilistically increase stochastic splice site usage. These findings reveal a distinct layer of noise in the regulation of gene expression.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Canonical and non-canonical miRNA degradation shapes state transitions and stemness in breast cancer
The EMBO Journal: Reconstitution of glycan-driven MHC-I recycling reveals calreticulin as mediator between TAPBPR and tapasin
The EMBO Journal: Nested TAD hierarchy defines cohesion zones on replicated chromosomes
The EMBO Journal: FAF1 and FAF2 enhance unfolding by p97-UFD1-NPL4 complex enabling rational design of p97 activators
Nature Cell Biology: An EZH2–SREBP2 axis promotes cholesterol biosynthesis and represents a noncanonical vulnerability in tumorigenesis
item.description: Kim et al. demonstrate a non-canonical function for EZH2 in modulating cholesterol metabolism and tumour development by interacting with SREBP2, which may be targeted by PROTACs to disrupt its oncogenic activity.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Selective decay of interferon mRNAs controls antiviral immunity and innate memory
item.description: Braun et al. identify that the canonical host mRNA deadenylation complex and an RNA-binding specificity factor, TTP, post-transcriptionally control antiviral interferon mRNAs through targeted deadenylation. Loss of mRNA decay machinery leads to a potent block against SARS-CoV-2 infection and can prime cells for innate immune memory.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Engineering editopes through programmable RNA editing toward tumor neoantigen generation
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Nucleosomes and IDRs suppress promiscuous GCN4 binding on minichromosomes
item.description: Wei et al. measure single-molecule kinetics of transcription factor GCN4 on purified yeast minichromosomes to reveal that both nucleosomes and transcription factor intrinsically disordered regions facilitate GCN4 target search on native chromatin by shortening its promiscuous binding.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Orally available Colivin traps TRPV3 in an inactive state and suppresses intestinal inflammation
The EMBO Journal: The calcium-binding protein CSE links Ca 2+ signaling with cell-cell communication in cyanobacteria
Molecular Cell: Molecular co-accessibility identifies coordinated regulation between distant cis-regulatory elements
item.description: Boulanger et al. study the coordination between cis-regulatory elements by simultaneously measuring their chromatin accessibility on the same kilobase-long DNA molecules. They show that co-accessibility identifies functionally dependent enhancers and promoters that have coordinated activity across cell types.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Chromatin condensates tune nuclear mechanosensing and preserve nuclear integrity to prevent cGAS activation
The EMBO Journal: Principles of ribosome-associated protein quality control during the synthesis of CFTR
Nature Cell Biology: Mega-enhancers compartmentalize transcriptionally active long genes in the brain
item.description: Zhao et al. describe an enhancer-dense nuclear microenvironment in the cerebellum that includes long neuronal genes and mega-enhancers. This microenvironment partly depends on the transcription factor Etv1 and is dynamic during neuronal maturation.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: In-situ cryo-ET of mouse embryos reveals cytoplasmic lattices contain ubiquitin-charged E2-E3 ligase assemblies
Nature Cell Biology: Targeting oncogenic FLT3 uncovers a ferroptosis vulnerability through selenocysteine recoding in acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: Li et al. report that FLT3 inhibition impairs selenoprotein translation and induces ferroptosis to suppress FLT3 -mutant leukaemia. This can be counteracted by dietary vitamin E, which may disrupt the efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors in treatment of acute myeloid leukaemia.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: The mitochondria enzyme OGDH defends against disulfidptosis by licensing METTL3-regulated NRF2 translation
item.description: Chen, Xu, Zhou, Wu et al. report that a citric acid cycle enzyme OGDH regulates METTL3 succinylation and its activation as an m6A reader, thereby modulating NRF2 translation, disulfidptosis evasion and tumour growth.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Allosteric switching of Ca 2+ permeability in the lysosomal ion channel TPC2 underpins biased agonist activation
The EMBO Journal: Pho84/GLUT2 are cellular myo -inositol exporters regulated by inositol pyrophosphates
Nature Cell Biology: CLOCK/BMAL1 interactome uncovers homeodomain factors as tissue regulators
item.description: Aygenli et al. map chromatin-bound CLOCK/BMAL1 protein complexes across three mouse tissues and uncover PROX1, HNF1B and HOXA5 as homeodomain cofactors that directly bind and co-occupy BMAL1 sites to establish tissue-specific circadian transcription.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Stromal cell senescence augments haematopoietic cell fitness in clonal haematopoiesis
item.description: Mistry et al. propose that Dnmt3a -mutant haematopoietic cells induce mesenchymal stromal cell senescence. Removal of senescent non-haematopoietic cells reduces Dnmt3a -mutant haematopoiesis.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Distinct amyloid-β filament fold in individuals with APP Flemish mutation
item.description: Brain samples from individuals with the rare APP Flemish mutation reveal a distinct amyloid-β filament fold that may help explain the accumulation of amyloid-β in blood vessels in inherited Alzheimer disease.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: BRD4 recruitment into HP1 condensates desilences transcription without erasure of repressive chromatin
item.description: Brandon, Robinson-Thiewes, Kaulage et al. report that targeted BRD4 recruitment enables transcription through H3K9me3/HP1-marked heterochromatin without erasing repressive marks, identifying condensate partitioning as a mechanism for gene desilencing.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: P-selectin delineates conserved functional heterogeneity in early hematopoietic stem cell aging in humans and mice
The EMBO Journal: Damage recognition by intestinal stem cells via Draper promotes adult Drosophila midgut regeneration
Molecular Cell: LZTFL1 rewires NADPH-glutathione metabolism to amplify ferroptosis
item.description: Xue et al. identify LZTFL1 as a key regulator of ferroptosis that rewires GSH metabolism by promoting G6PD oxidation. GSH depletion enhances LZTFL1 translation, forming a feedforward circuit that amplifies ferroptosis. Restoring LZTFL1 re-sensitizes cisplatin-resistant tumors, highlighting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Torsins organize CLCC1 assembly to safeguard ER bilayer and lipid homeostasis
item.description: Chen and colleagues identify CLCC1 as the functional substrate downstream of torsin AAA+ ATPases. TorsinA depletion disrupts CLCC1’s oligomeric state and triggers massive lipid deposition within the ER. Importantly, ectopic expression of CLCC1 overcomes torsinA loss and fully reverses the lipid mis-deposition.

item.title: Molecular Cell: The dystonia-associated Torsin1A sustains CLCC1 function in membrane fusion of the nuclear envelope for NPC biogenesis
item.description: Maslennikova et al. identify the ER membrane protein CLCC1 as an interaction partner of the dystonia-linked AAA+ ATPase Torsin1A. Torsin1A sustains the function of CLCC1, which is proposed to facilitate fusion of the nuclear envelope during NPC biogenesis by forming an oligomer that promotes lipid bilayer approach and remodeling.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Membrane lipid composition and rapid endocytic retrieval modulate Wingless secretion
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Variant characterization in the intrinsically disordered human proteome
item.description: Proteome-wide prediction and structural modeling of disordered protein interaction interfaces advance characterization of disease-associated variants in disordered protein regions.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Factors modulating the assembly of human β 2 -adrenergic receptor–β-arrestin complexes
item.description: Wilhelm, Pluhackova and colleagues show how ligand binding, receptor phosphorylation and membrane interactions, including PIP 2 , drive the assembly of human β 2 -adrenergic receptor–β-arrestin complexes, providing insight into structural mechanisms regulating GPCR signaling.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Protein thiol alterations drive pathologic liquid–liquid phase separation in the aging brain
item.description: Vignane et al. show that age-related protein oxidation disrupts normal brain protein organization, promoting harmful condensates and aggregation linked to neurodegeneration, whereas hydrogen sulfide-driven persulfidation counteracts these effects.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: NF-κB/RelA signaling required for CD40-induced humoral immunity depends on specific NEMO lysine residues in mice
The EMBO Journal: Polo/PLK1 phosphorylation relieves Centrosomin/Cnn autoinhibition to promote centrosome scaffold assembly
Nature Cell Biology: The glycolytic enzyme PGAM1 functions as a metabolic–autophagy checkpoint to coordinate growth and stress tolerance
item.description: Zhang, Zhao, Liang et al. report that, independent of its catalytic function, the glycolytic enzyme PGAM1 acts as a scaffold protein to regulate autophagy activation, thereby modulating cellular homeostasis and stress response.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: The Arabidopsis SPFH protein HIR2 modulates receptor signaling and plasma membrane organization
Nature Cell Biology: Nuclear class 3 PI3K co-activates fasting-specific chromatin remodelling
item.description: Henneman et al. report an unexpected role for class 3 PI3K (PI3K-3) acting as a transcriptional co-activator during fasting. They show that nuclear PI3K-3 co-activates the methyltransferase Set1/COMPASS complex to promote H3K4me3 deposition.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Cancer stem cells are hyper-responsive sensors of the tumour microenvironment and regulate metastasis dynamics through YAP/TAZ
item.description: Using a dynamic fluorescent reporter, Tang et al. demonstrate that cancer stem cells are hyper-responsive to microenvironmental cues, which they sense and adapt to through YAP/TAZ signalling, thereby playing an essential role in breast cancer lung metastasis.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural mechanism of TOPBP1 activating the ATR–ATRIP replication checkpoint kinase
item.description: Li et al. present cryo-EM structures of the ATR–ATRIP complex bound to the ATR-activating domains of TOPBP1 and ETAA1; these reveal distinct binding modes and allosteric mechanism of activation for TOPBP1 and ETAA1.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Direct coupling of human TOM and TIM22 complexes drives mitochondrial carrier import
item.description: Liu, Cai and colleagues show that the human TOM–TIM22 supercomplex acts a translocation unit that directly couples mitochondrial carrier import across the outer and inner membranes, in contrast to the independent function of the complexes in yeast.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: RAD54L coordinates the nucleolar DNA damage response to maintain rDNA stability
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: PLA2G2F suppresses ferroptosis through phospholipid remodeling
item.description: Hu et al. identify the secretory phospholipase PLA2G2F as an endoplasmic reticulum-resident ferroptosis suppressor in bladder cancer and provide evidence that PLA2G2F acts on ether-linked phospholipids containing polyunsaturated fatty acids, reducing the pool of these peroxidation-prone phospholipids.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Tripartite ER-mitochondria-lipid droplets contact sites control adipocyte metabolic flexibility
The EMBO Journal: FUS controls muscle differentiation through phase separation-mediated recruitment of the transcription factors MEF2 and ETV5
Molecular Cell: Yeast Rad55–Rad57–SHU paralog complex dynamically promotes Rad51 filament formation
item.description: Koo et al. show how the yeast Rad51 paralog complex Rad55–Rad57–SHU promotes homologous recombination. Cryo-EM structures reveal that Rad55–Rad57 recruits Rad51 to ssDNA to seed filament formation, while ATP hydrolysis promotes paralog complex turnover.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural and functional basis of antinociceptive action of χ-conotoxin AoIA at the noradrenaline transporter
item.description: Belleza, Zhang and colleagues showed that the χ-conotoxin χ-AoIA, a venom-derived peptide, reduces pain in mice by blocking the norepinephrine transporter more effectively than other similar peptides.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Proteolytic activation of executioner caspase-3 and -7 regulates different physiological processes in mice
Nature Cell Biology: Mitochondrial-derived vesicles drive budding-type fission of damaged lysosomes
item.description: Luo et al. describe a budding type of lysosome fission linked to delivery of MFF from mitochondrial-derived vesicles to lysosomes. MFF recruits DRP1 for membrane scission. This axis restores lysosome function during hypoxia–reoxygenation stress.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Atg23 prevents aberrant fusion of Atg9 vesicles during delivery to autophagosome formation sites
The EMBO Journal: Vps1 drives membrane constriction and fission necessary for endosomal protein sorting
The EMBO Journal: Reactive oxygen species stimulate Paneth cell plasticity and diminish antimicrobial function
Molecular Cell: Thermo-sensing mechanisms of splicing control by nuclear stress bodies
item.description: Ueno et al. show that the phosphorylation of CLK1 functions as a molecular switch controlling its temperature-dependent localization to nuclear stress bodies. This regulation is mediated by a multilayered thermosensing mechanism involving PPP1R2, an intrinsically disordered thermosensor regulating PP1-mediated dephosphorylation during stress, and RIOK2-dependent rephosphorylation during recovery, coordinating temperature-dependent pre-mRNA splicing.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Conformational plasticity of human acid-sensing ion channel 1a
item.description: Using cryo-electron microscopy, Cahill, Hartfield et al. identified six structural states of human acid-sensing ion channel 1a, revealing how acidic conditions and peptide toxins regulate channel activation and desensitization through conformational flexibility.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Developmental priming of adult proteostasis and longevity by NuA4 complex activity in early life
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: ESCRT-III assembles around mis-segregated DNA to protect genome stability
item.description: The authors show that persistent ultrafine DNA bridges become coated by membranes and the ESCRT-III proteins CHMP1B and IST1, which protect the genome within from damage.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Metabolic buffering restricts phenotype switching in melanoma
The EMBO Journal: A conserved basic motif mediates membrane anchoring and TRAF2 recruitment across costimulatory TNFRs
Nature Cell Biology: Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers endothelial progenitor-like remodelling driving human coronary atherosclerosis progression
item.description: Yao, Li, Gai et al. profile normal coronary artery and early and advanced coronary atherosclerosis samples from humans using single-cell transcriptomics and identify a progenitor-like endothelial subtype with functional implications in disease progression

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: CST complex promotes second-strand synthesis in break-induced replication
item.description: Here Thakre, Wang and Liu and colleagues show that the Cdc13–Stn1–Ten1 complex helps cells to repair broken DNA by enabling synthesis of the second DNA strand during break-induced replication, a process important for genome stability and telomere maintenance in some cancers.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Spalt-related is an inhibitor of mTORC1-mediated growth activated by the integrated stress response
The EMBO Journal: CDK8 remodels the tumor microenvironment and promotes resistance to KRAS G12D inhibitors and daraxonrasib in PDAC
Nature Cell Biology: Decoding stage-specific functions of PRC2 in early embryogenesis uncovers roles in preimplantation development and primordial germ cell fate
item.description: Zhou, Wang et al. dissect the role of PRC2 in early embryogenesis through inducible degradation of EED, a core PRC2 subunit, and report that PRC2 is required for proper maternal-to-zygotic transition and promotes epiblast specification.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Oncogenic EGFR rewires STING-TBK1 signalosomes to license DNA damage tolerance in NSCLC
The EMBO Journal: Mechanical constraints regulate embryonic stem cell mitosis in the developing brain
Molecular Cell: A conserved mechanism of membrane fusion in nuclear pore complex assembly
item.description: Fischer et al. uncover a fundamental mechanism of membrane fusion during nuclear pore complex (NPC) assembly. Brl1 and Brr6 form ring-shaped, membrane-remodeling complexes that interact and bridge the nuclear envelope at NPC-assembly sites to mediate fusion. This pathway is conserved in humans via the metazoan fusogen CLCC1.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Cytoplasmic lattices store developmentally poised degradative and cytoskeletal complexes in mammalian eggs
item.description: Li et al. obtain high-resolution, native structures revealing that cytoplasmic lattices in mammalian eggs organize and store degradative and cytoskeletal complexes for early embryonic development.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Inhibition of lagging strand replication by G-rich telomeric DNA and the shelterin subunit POT1
The EMBO Journal: Alterations in chromatin organization promote totipotent-like features in a DPPA2/DUX-dependent manner
The EMBO Journal: Structure and receptor recognition of type-II feline infectious peritonitis virus spike glycoprotein
Nature Cell Biology: CD44 restricts EGFR mobility to polarize cytoskeletal signalling modules driving bleb-based migration
item.description: Jha et al. show that the transmembrane protein CD44 restricts EGFR mobility to maintain an EGFR–PI3K–Rac gradient during bleb-based cell migration.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Evolutionarily conserved short linear motifs drive actin filament binding
item.description: Paraschiakos, Yuan et al., using a computational pipeline, identify the short linear actin filament-binding motif (SFM) as an evolutionarily conserved actin filament-binding motif present in 103 human proteins.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Promoter reinforcement supports transcriptional resilience in drug-resistant cancer
item.description: Kameswaran et al. show that cancer cells can restore gene expression after TEAD inhibition by shifting control from enhancers to promoters, a process termed ‘promoter reinforcement’, enabling transcription despite disrupted promoter–enhancer communication.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Distinct ATRX functions cooperate with 9-1-1 and CST complexes to safeguard replication and telomere integrity
item.description: Segura-Bayona et al. uncover genetically separable ATRX functions that independently safeguard telomeres and genome replication, revealing how CST and 9-1-1 pathways suppress accumulation of toxic single-stranded DNA and preserve chromosome integrity.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural basis of asymmetric transcription through a composite nucleosome formed by a hexasome and an octasome
item.description: This study shows that RNA polymerase II traverses overlapping dinucleosomes (OLDNs) with direction-dependent efficiency. Cryo-EM structures further reveal how RNA polymerase II rearranges OLDNs, promoting directional transcription.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structurally defining neurokinin selectivity to improve NK2R agonists
item.description: The researchers used cryo-electron microscopy to map how synthetic agonists bind to the neurokinin 2 receptor to reveal the features that make them selective. These studies are a key step toward developing future obesity therapies that boost energy expenditure.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Cis and trans regulatory mechanisms of extrachromosomal DNA segregation
item.description: Xie et al. demonstrate that extrachromosomal DNA tethering to mitotic chromosomes is in part mediated by H3K27ac-marked chromatin, associated chromatin binders and transcription-associated cofactors.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Catalytic activation of human Argonaute 2 requires RNA duplex deformation
item.description: Human Argonaute 2 requires distortion of the paired small interfering RNA (siRNA)–target RNA duplex, not just base pairing, to cleave targets. Structures show how RNA shape and key residues enable catalysis, explaining why some siRNAs are more effective.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural basis of AtCas9 recognition of PAM mutants in underwound DNA topology
item.description: Cryo-EM structures of AtCas9 bound to underwound minicircle DNA reveal how DNA topology relaxes PAM recognition through topology-dependent interactions, providing a structural basis for near-PAMless CRISPR targeting.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Mediator subunit MED4 enforces metastatic dormancy in breast cancer
item.description: Bae et al. identify MED4 as a regulator of tumour dormancy from a genome-wide CRISPR screen, and show that loss of MED4 alters the enhancer landscape and induces extracellular matrix remodelling to drive metastatic relapse in breast cancer.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Lysosome-derived methylated arginine is a signalling metabolite controlling the lipidome
item.description: Nguyen et al. show that accumulation of dimethylarginine in lysosomes in disease models is associated with lipotoxicity and lipid droplet abundance.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Integrated stress response couples mitochondrial fitness with lineage reprogramming to drive cancer evolution
item.description: Diao, Zou et al. demonstrate that activation of the integrated stress response drives lineage dedifferentiation and tumour progression in lung adenocarcinoma, associated with aberrant mitochondrial function and metabolic fitness.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: ERO1a fosters glioblastoma aggressiveness and metabolic flexibility by regulating mitochondria-associated membrane dynamics
item.description: Bassot, Violy, Gorka, Cigalotto and colleagues identify ERO1a as a mitochondria-associated membrane protein that regulates calcium flux and mitochondria bioenergetics, which may be potentially targeted to inhibit glioblastoma growth in vivo.
